cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the strength you carry is moving outward by measure.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Say the heading you want for the group's welfare in a sentence, and take a real step on it this week. Other good directions can wait their turn, unsteered.
cells.core:
When the group's weight lands and you can already see how it all fits, your strength goes out where it's needed and comes back undrained. You read the shape of the whole thing from where you stand and put support exactly where it holds — no pushing, no hoarding. That's the balance working.

For the next stretch, aim your effort at a single direction instead of surveying all of them. Decide it from what you want, not from the list's logic, and steer that way for a few days. Being pointed one way will feel like losing sight of the rest, and that's the cost. A whole puzzle doesn't need solving this week — its next step does.
cells.sheetLine: Support flows out by measure, because you can see the pattern.
cells.verb: channeling shared strength outward to the people who need it
cells.place: standing just outside the working group, where you can see how it fits together

cells.tense: You will be bearing down on a load that has not reached you yet, forcing support ahead of the moment it is needed.
cells.act: let the inner compass decide the small case
cells.ask: Let your sense of what's fair settle a small unbalance near you — something owed, a share unpaid — without weighing who notices. That case only; hold the larger verdicts back.
cells.core:
The support you give is still going outward, but it is being sent ahead of schedule. You see the whole pattern so clearly that you start supplying what hasn't been asked for yet, bearing weight nobody handed you, bracing against a shortfall that may not arrive at all. What's meant to be shared by measure turns into you holding all the slack.

Under it is a fairness you feel fast — a quick verdict about what should be given, and by whom, before the moment has finished arriving. Slow that down by letting your private sense of what's owed decide a small case and nothing more. That keeps the read of the pattern; it just sets it back down in the present. A compass used on a small case is not a court.

cells.tense: The support that used to move outward stood down, and you left the room before you left the role.
cells.act: engage the hard part on purpose and see what holds
cells.ask: Name the commitment you'd still claim in public, then meet the part you've been avoiding — deliberately, once. Not a fresh promise; one contact with the friction, and notice what held.
cells.core:
Strength and its sharing are still yours, but they aren't arriving here. From the place where you can see how everything fits, you read the pattern and then don't step in — the group's weight is visible and unmoved by you. What would be given by measure is stalled, and the shape of the whole keeps being seen by someone who isn't acting on it.

What's needed is smaller than a change of heart. Name what you claim still matters, then deliberately meet the hard part of it once — the friction itself, not the feeling about it. What you are committed to shows up in that contact or it doesn't. Either answer is useful, and pushing more support into the quiet place won't move it.

cells.tense: The support between people is moving right now and you are not counting yourself among the ones who move it.
cells.act: turn toward the one direction and stop surveying
cells.ask: By your own account you are a bystander. So aim your weight at a heading the group is actually moving in — pick it and go, rather than reading through all the options first, and own it as chosen.
cells.core:
Wherever you are, support keeps flowing between people — things get supplied, gaps get covered, someone's weight gets taken up — and you tell it as something that happens, not something you do. The pattern is read. The strength is being shared. You are just not in the story of it. By your own telling you stand outside the group, watching it hold.

Claim a heading. Of everything the group is moving toward, pick the one you are actually for and put your weight there on purpose, so the pattern you read and the direction you feed are the same thing. What you have done gets named by you, to you. Noticing is not a new offer here; it is the one already running, returned.
cells.sheetLine: The support is flowing. You call yourself a bystander.
cells.verb: channeling shared strength outward to the people who need it
cells.place: standing just outside the working group, where you can see how it fits together

attempts.check: The record never says the person is good at seeing whole patterns; the seat only says where Support landed, and seeing the true shape of a group is one reading the draw does not supply. A reader could say they are simply the one who always ends up carrying supplies for everyone, without any insight into the pattern. The asks are small, private and optional, so they hold whether the read is right or not — the Orientation acts need no group at hand. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line that congratulates them on their perceptiveness instead of showing them what they are carrying.
